name: Maacah
overview: Maacah was a male member of the tribe of Simeon, known primarily as the father of Shephatiah according to 1 Chronicles 27:16. Beyond this paternal role, Scripture provides limited information about him. His identity is firmly rooted in his tribal affiliation and familial connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Maacah is a proper name that may mean 'dull' or 'stupid,' though this is not explicitly stated as given by God. This single name is the only recorded designation for this individual in Scripture, without additional titles or meanings.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Maacah as the father of Shephatiah and explicitly identifies him as a descendant of the tribe of Simeon. No other family relationships are documented beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Maacah's significance in the biblical narrative is primarily genealogical, serving as a link in the lineage of Simeon through his son Shephatiah. His mention in 1 Chronicles 27:16 situates him within the tribal organization and leadership structure of Israel, underscoring the importance of family lines in God's providential plan. While not a prominent figure in events or teachings, his recorded lineage contributes to the historical and spiritual heritage of God's people.
